name: Windows — UAC Bypass via Auto-Elevated LOLBin
description:
Attacker objective
Elevate from a medium-integrity to a high-integrity process without a consent prompt by abusing a Windows auto-elevating binary (UAC bypass).

Attack logic
Several trusted Windows binaries auto-elevate and can be hijacked (via registry/COM manipulation) to launch an attacker process elevated. The tell is an auto-elevating binary spawning a command interpreter or scripting host.

Why this detection works
Process-creation lineage links the auto-elevating parent to a shell/scripting child on the same event, a combination that does not occur in normal use.

False positives
Rare legitimate automation that launches a shell from one of these binaries.

Tuning
Allowlist verified parent/child pairs if a legitimate workflow triggers it.

Required telemetry
Process creation with parent process: Sysmon Event ID 1 and Windows Security 4688 (process.parent.name).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The parent (auto-elevated binary) launched a shell/scripting child — a UAC-bypass pattern.
2. Review the child command line for the follow-on action; investigate the user and host.
3. Confirm whether elevation was legitimate; if not, treat the host as compromised.
false_positives: Rare legitimate automation that launches a shell from one of these binaries.
query: process where event.code in ("1","4688") and process.parent.name in~ ("fodhelper.exe","eventvwr.exe","sdclt.exe","computerdefaults.exe","cmstp.exe","wsreset.exe","slui.exe","changepk.exe","dccw.exe") and process.name in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","hh.exe")
